findings.claim: The 12-mark question is called a 'Discuss' question throughout the unit: practice question 5 in every lesson is typed '12 marks — Discuss a Statement' with the stem 'Discuss this statement.', and the exam tips and two collapsibles say '12-mark Discuss questions'.
findings.truth: Discuss is not an Edexcel command word. The spec's command-word appendix lists State, Outline, Describe, Explain and Evaluate only; the 12-mark AO2 command word is Evaluate. 'Discuss this statement' is another board's wording.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3: Command Words (command-word table, Evaluate = 12 marks, AO2); spec assessment overview p.4 (four questions, each numbered (a) to (d))

findings.claim: Every lesson's practice question 2 is typed '3 marks — Describe' with a Describe stem (e.g. 'Describe what Christians believe about the resurrection of Jesus.').
findings.truth: Paper 1 sets four questions, one per section, each with parts (a) Outline three (3), (b) Explain two (4), (c) Explain two with a source of wisdom and authority (5), (d) Evaluate (12) — 96 marks plus 6 SPaG = 102. There is no 3-mark Describe part, and the spec's command-word table puts Describe at 4 marks. Reshaped as Outline three; the existing mark schemes already award 1 mark per point up to 3.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview p.4 and Assessment information p.22 (1 hour 45, 102 marks, four questions (a)-(d), SPaG minimum 5%); spec Appendix 3 command-word table

findings.claim: “Examiners reward balance: develop at least two reasons on each side…”
findings.truth: An invented examiner claim. The requirement for both sides comes from the (d) question's own instructions, which ask for reasoned arguments in support and for a different point of view. Rewritten to say that.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 note on Evaluate questions (additional instructions given to students for all Evaluate questions); house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: “John 3:16–21” is given four times as the prescribed salvation passage — bolded in the Key Fact, in its revision tip, in the takeaways as a ‘key biblical anchor’, and in the exam tip.
findings.truth: The spec names John 3:10–21 (with Acts 4:8–12) for salvation. The passage quoted and described is unchanged; only the reference range was wrong. The two practice mark schemes offer John 3:16-21 as one acceptable source example, which still earns credit, so those were left alone.

findings.claim: “Students are expected to compare Christian eschatology with another tradition — the most likely comparison in the exam is Islam or Catholic Christianity.”
findings.truth: The starred comparison for 1.6 is with one other religion practised in Great Britain — Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism or Sikhism. Catholic Christianity is a different option of this same paper (1A), not a comparison religion; divergent Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant views are a separate requirement inside Christianity.
findings.evidence: spec Area of Study 1B overview (comparison list, 1.6* and 2.1*); paper codes 1RA0/1A-1C

findings.claim: “The Anglican Thirty-Nine Articles deliberately leave room for both views” (memorialist and spiritual presence) on the Eucharist.
findings.truth: Article XXVIII takes a position. It says transubstantiation cannot be proved by holy Writ and is repugnant to the plain words of Scripture, that the body of Christ is given, taken and eaten in the Supper only after a heavenly and spiritual manner, and that the means of receiving is faith. Replaced with that, which also hands the student a citable source for the 5-mark part.
findings.evidence: Thirty-Nine Articles, Article XXVIII (Wikisource, Articles of Religion); spec 2.2 names the 39 Articles XXV-XXXVI

findings.claim: “This lesson covers Sections 3 and 4 of the spec — Sources of Wisdom and Forms of Expression. Both sections appear as (c) and (d) questions in your exam.”
findings.truth: Wrong paper structure. Each of the four sections gets its own whole question, numbered (a) to (d). Sections 3 and 4 each carry a 3-mark, a 4-mark, a 5-mark and a 12-mark part — half the paper. A student told these sections only appear as (c) and (d) parts would revise a quarter of the paper as if it were an add-on.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview p.4 (four sections must all be studied; four questions, each numbered (a) to (d)); Assessment information p.22

findings.claim: “Taize attracts hundreds of thousands of young Christians annually” (12-mark mark scheme).
findings.truth: Taize receives over 100,000 young people a year. 'Hundreds of thousands' overstates it by roughly a factor of three.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Taize Community (over 100,000 young people each year)

findings.claim: Inside the theodicy collapsible the book title is wrapped in markdown asterisks: (*Evil and the God of Love*, 1966).
findings.truth: The asterisks render as literal characters in the lesson; every other citation of the title uses <em>. Cosmetic, not mark-affecting, so left alone under the style exclusion.

findings.claim: Purgatory is described as “the Catholic and some Orthodox teaching”, and the mark scheme accepts “Catholic (and some Orthodox) Christians believe in purgatory”.
findings.truth: Orthodox churches do not teach purgatory as a doctrine, though they pray for the dead and accept an intermediate state. The hedge 'some' keeps this defensible, but a student who drops the hedge would be wrong. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 1.6 (39 Articles and Catholic teachings named; Orthodox not named for purgatory)

findings.claim: The 5-mark mark scheme offers “Musicum Sacrum (1967 Vatican document on sacred music)” as a named source.
findings.truth: The real document is Musicam Sacram (1967); the spec itself prints 'Musicum Sacrum' in 4.7. Two options: (a) leave it, so the lesson matches the wording a student will meet on the spec and in board materials; (b) correct it to Musicam Sacram and lose that match. The date 1967 is right either way. Recommend (a) — leave it, and let the spec-currency audit raise the spec typo instead.
findings.evidence: spec 1B Section 4, point 4.7; Musicam Sacram, Instruction on Music in the Liturgy, 5 March 1967
findings.ruling: Leave: matches the spec wording students meet.

findings.claim: Galatians 3:28 quoted as “there is neither male nor female … you are all one in Christ Jesus”.
findings.truth: The NIV reads 'nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus'; the quoted form is the older KJV/RSV wording. The lesson already flags the verse as not named in the spec and marks the cut with an ellipsis, so no mark is at stake.

summary: Two structural exam errors run through all six lessons: the 12-mark part is called a Discuss question (Edexcel's command word is Evaluate) and every lesson carries a 3-mark Describe practice question, a form this paper does not set. Content and scripture are otherwise strong — NIV quotations, creed wording, 39 Articles citations, dates and every knowledge-check answer key checked out — with six single-lesson corrections, the worst being lesson 6's claim that Sections 3 and 4 appear only as (c) and (d) questions.
